body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, who is in the form of a youth!

children.translated_text: From existence, non-existence does not arise; nor does it arise from non-existence.

children.text: bhāva utpaddyate nityaṃ bhābo bhrāntiḥ khapuṣpavat // 1 //
children.translated_text: Existence appears to arise constantly, yet existence is an illusion, like a flower in the sky. (1)

children.text: sati dharme nabhastulye khatulyaṃ jāyate param /
children.translated_text: When a <s>dharma</s> exists that is like the sky, what arises beyond it is likewise sky-like;
all arise dependently, equal to the sky — therefore, existence is endowed with non-existence. (2)

children.text: sbabhāvataḥ karma nāsti heturnāsti phalaṃ na ca /
children.translated_text: By inherent nature, action does not exist, nor does a cause, nor a result;

children.text: na viddyata idaṃ sarbaṃ loko nāsti na bhañjanam // 3 //
children.translated_text: all this is not found — the world does not exist, nor does its destruction. (3)
And that entity which is unborn — how could it produce another?

children.text: lokaḥ prathamato 'jātaḥ kenāpi na hi nirmitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The world is primordially unborn, not constructed by anyone;
like the city of <s>Somasiṃha</s>, the world wanders in meaninglessness. (4)
The world arises from conceptualization, and conceptualization arises from mind;
mind indeed depends upon the body — therefore, the body should be examined. (5)

children.text: rūpaṃ śūnyaṃ vedanā niḥsvabhāvā saṃjñā nāste nāsti saṃskārabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Form is empty, feeling is without inherent nature, perception does not exist, nor does the reality of formations;

children.text: bhūtaṃ hitvā cittacaitte ca nastastasmātkāyaḥ kalpahīnasvabhāvaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: even the elements having been set aside, mind and mental factors too perish — therefore, the body's nature is devoid of conceptual construction. (6)

children.text: citta nāsti na dharmāste na kāyo nāpi dhātavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mind does not exist, <s>dharmas</s> do not exist, neither body nor elements exist;
this making into non-duality is declared by the wise to be reality. (7)
All this is without support; the supportless has been proclaimed.
Having made the mind supportless, the supportless is realized. (8)
When generosity, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and the rest are well cultivated,
in a very short time, one will attain supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). (9)
Abiding in skillful means and wisdom, one should nurture beings with compassion;
one will quickly obtain omniscient knowledge — there is no doubt about this. (10)
All this is mere name, established upon mere designation;
apart from the designation, no designatum is found. (11)
All <s>dharmas</s> are nameless, proclaimed to be without self.
These <s>dharmas</s> are unreal, arisen from conceptualization;

children.text: kalpanā sāpi śūnyeyaṃ yayā śūnyeti kalpitāḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: that very conceptualization by which things are conceived as empty is itself empty. (12)
'The eye sees forms' — this is what the teacher of reality states;
it is declared to be the conventional truth for the world that holds false conceit. (13)
Where the Guide illuminates that seeing arises through the aggregate of conditions,
the wise one declared that to be the figurative level of the ultimate. (14)

children.text: na cakṣuḥ prekṣate rūpaṃ mano dharmānnvetti ca /
children.translated_text: The eye does not perceive form, nor does the mind comprehend <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: etattu paraṃ satyaṃ lokasya viṣayo na yat // 15 //
children.translated_text: this indeed is the ultimate truth, which is not the domain of the world. (15)

children.text: cakṣurnāsti na rūpañca dṛśyaṃ nāsti na manaskriyā /
children.translated_text: The eye does not exist, nor form; the visible does not exist, nor the activity of mind.

children.text: cittaṃ svapnasamaṃ bhrāntiḥ sarvaṃ na sadasanna ca // 16 //
children.translated_text: Mind is like a dream, an illusion — all is neither existent nor non-existent. (16)

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhavasaṅkrāntiparikathā</s> (Discourse on the Transition of Existence), composed by the master, the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, is complete.
